relations.instance_semantics: Process is governed by policies or rules
Policy can be expressed through constraints or rules
Projection or disclosure policy specializes the generic governed policy with output-shape semantics
relations.rationale: Keep generic policy identity authority lifecycle and conflict rules in WM-KNW-012

model.name: Legal Instrument / Norm
model.purpose: Represent an authority-backed legal instrument and the norms expressed by its addressable source fragments, independent of storage and interface format.
model.scope_statement: Owns legal-work, expression, manifestation, source, provision and norm linkage; instrument class; authority and legal-basis references; structure and citations; authenticity and provenance; deontic assertions; lifecycle, temporal applicability, interpretation, access and projections. Organizations, lawmaking procedures, cases, enforcement events, affected parties, places and generic document storage remain external masters.
in_scope: Legal work, expression, manifestation, item, authoritative source, provision and norm identity
Authority, class, structure, citation, normative meaning, lifecycle, time, applicability, conflict and provenance
Authentication, consolidation, controlled disclosure, retention, interoperability and safe agent operations
out_of_scope: Issuing organization, legislative or administrative procedure and generic document repository masters
Court or arbitration case, enforcement event, affected person, asset and place masters
Automated legal advice, universally binding interpretation or substantive law common to every jurisdiction

boundary_notes.distinction: Authorities are external organizations referenced in a specific legal capacity; the legal instrument owns neither their identity nor governance.
The process produces adoption and publication evidence; the instrument aggregate preserves outputs and lifecycle assertions but not the workflow master.
A case may interpret, invalidate or apply an instrument, but its parties, procedure, evidence and decision lifecycle remain a separate model.
A policy or rule may lack legal-source authority; this aggregate requires explicit legal-source, jurisdiction and competent-authority bindings.
Files and records are manifestations or evidence items; they do not replace authority-qualified legal-work identity or normative semantics.

functions.name: Add expression or manifestation
functions.description: Bind a language expression, file manifestation or held item to the same legal work.
preconditions: work and derivation resolve
effects: the new representation is separately identifiable and attributable

functions.name: Authenticate authoritative source
functions.description: Record publisher, publication act, authenticity evidence, digest and copy status.
preconditions: publisher role and evidence are known
effects: official and unofficial copies remain distinguishable

functions.name: Address provision and citation
functions.description: Mint or bind stable subdivision identities and resolve static or dynamic citations.
preconditions: source versions and numbering history resolve
effects: provisions stay citable across rendition and renumbering

functions.name: Bind norm to source
functions.description: Attach a structured or formal norm to exact source fragments with author, method and confidence.
preconditions: source fragments and expression version resolve
effects: formal semantics remain attributable and contestable

functions.name: Record legal lifecycle event
functions.description: Append adoption, publication, commencement, suspension, repeal, expiry or correction evidence.
preconditions: competence, affected scope and times validate
effects: state changes without overwriting prior assertions

functions.name: Construct consolidated view
functions.description: Apply cited modifications to create a dated non-authoritative or authority-qualified consolidated expression.
preconditions: all applied sources and unresolved conflicts are explicit
effects: the view remains distinct from original acts

functions.name: Assess applicability as assertion
functions.description: Produce a source-qualified applicability result for stated facts without claiming universal legal judgment.
preconditions: versions, jurisdiction and authority scope resolve
effects: reasoning inputs and unresolved conflicts stay inspectable

functions.name: Issue interoperability view

functions.name: Retire or supersede legal work

model.name: Policy / Rule
model.purpose: Provide the format-neutral context an agent needs to identify, classify, compose, govern, version and interpret an executable or interpretable normative statement, while delegating condition expression, runtime evaluation, enforcement and governed-process semantics to referenced models.
model.scope_statement: Describes an individual normative statement (policy, policy set, or atomic rule slot) as a governed record: identity and version identity, deontic or alethic force, issuing authority and mandate, applicability scope, rule-slot structure, declared precedence and conflict strategy, registered derogations, lifecycle and temporal validity, provenance and source-provision mapping, declared standard alignments, and record classification and retention. Storage- and interface-neutral: JSON, YAML, Markdown, XML, RDF, Git trees, MCP surfaces and document databases are manifestations of one record. Carries references and binding metadata for constraint expressions but never the expression grammar, and never renders, executes, enforces or logs a decision.
in_scope: Identity, naming, citation forms and version identity, separated into abstract work, dated expression and rendered manifestation.
Deontic modality (obligation, permission, prohibition, right), alethic-versus-deontic classification, enforcement level and defeasibility.
Instrument genre and binding form: legislation, regulation, standard, internal directive, set, offer, agreement.
Issuing authority, mandate, adoption-decision reference, and post-issuance record ownership and stewardship roles.
Applicability scope: jurisdiction, territory, subject-matter competence, in-scope parties, target resources, governed actions and contextual conditions.
Rule-slot inventory, atomicity, policy-set containment and inheritance.
References and binding metadata for externally owned constraint or rule expressions, plus subject-specific parameter values and tailoring.
Declared precedence: combining or hit-policy strategy identifiers, conflict terms and pairwise superiority relations.
Registered exceptions, waivers and derogations, and recorded alternative interpretations and known contradictions.
Lifecycle states, amendment, supersession and repeal; in-force, efficacy and applicability intervals with event time and record time.
Provenance, derivation, attribution and mapping from rule slots to authoritative source provisions.
Declared standard alignments, structural well-formedness requirements, manifestation integrity, record classification, retention declaration and disposition class.
out_of_scope: Constraint and rule expression grammar, operator and operand vocabularies, and logical composition semantics (WM-KNW-013).
Runtime policy evaluation, decision rendering, obligation discharge, enforcement actions and decision results (referenced decision or enforcement runtime).
Audit-trail entities, event streams and log storage for evaluation, enforcement or access.
Process, activity and task definitions and their execution state (WM-ACT-003).
Projection, disclosure and output-shape semantics of specialised disclosure policies (WM-XCT-003).
Party, organisation, resource and place master data.
Compliance risk assessment, control-effectiveness measurement and non-compliance case handling.
Sanction computation, penalty scales and litigation records.
Storage engines, serialization formats, access interfaces and repository mechanics.
Cryptographic signing ceremonies and PKI trust management.

boundary_notes.distinction: The condition itself (left operand, operator, right operand, logical operands, refinements) and its own lifecycle are owned there. This model carries only the reference, the binding point, the expression-language reference and subject-specific parameter values.

boundary_notes.neighbor: Referenced decision or enforcement runtime (XACML PDP/PEP, ABAC access decision function)
boundary_notes.distinction: Evaluation, decision rendering, obligation discharge and decision logging are runtime concerns. This model declares which combining or hit-policy strategy applies and where its normative definition lives; it never evaluates or enforces.
Activities, tasks, sequence and execution state are owned there. The governance edge is authored by WM-ACT-003; this model only records applicability pointers to governed processes.

Output-shape, redaction-transform and disclosure-projection semantics are specialised there. Generic identity, authority, lifecycle and conflict machinery is retained here, as the relation rationale requires.
Compliance risk evaluation, monitoring, reporting and non-compliance handling sit in a compliance management model. This model holds the obligation statement and its governance metadata only.

Manifestation storage, format conversion, digital preservation and disposal execution belong to records management. This model holds work/expression identity, retention declaration, disposition class and tombstone.
Domain grouping, portfolio taxonomy and cross-policy programme governance sit with the parent. This model describes one normative statement instance.

sources.title: ODRL Information Model 2.2
sources.relevance: Normative policy/rule structure: Policy uid MUST, Set/Offer/Agreement subclasses, Permission/Prohibition/Duty, action, target, assigner/assignee, constraint and refinement placement, conflict term (perm/prohibit/invalid), inheritFrom, profile conformance, dc:isReplacedBy handling.

sources.title: eXtensible Access Control Markup Language (XACML) Version 3.0
sources.relevance: PolicySet/Policy/Rule containment with required PolicySetId, PolicyId, RuleId and Version; RuleCombiningAlgId and PolicyCombiningAlgId; Target and Condition separation; PolicyIssuer; VersionMatch; and the PDP/PEP/PAP/PIP separation that fixes the evaluation boundary.

sources.title: LegalRuleML Core Specification Version 1.0
sources.relevance: Deontic operators (obligation, permission, prohibition, right), strong versus weak permission, defeasibility and Override superiority relations, Authority and Jurisdiction, LegalSources/appliesSource provision mapping, TemporalCharacteristic for in-force/efficacy/applicability, Alternatives and Context.

sources.title: Akoma Ntoso Version 1.0 Part 1: XML Vocabulary
sources.relevance: FRBR Work/Expression/Manifestation/Item split, IRI naming convention, lifecycle element with dated events, originalVersion/singleVersion/multipleVersions, @start/@end/@startEfficacy/@endEfficacy, amendment and repeal status values, and point-in-time consolidation.

sources.title: Semantics of Business Vocabulary and Business Rules (SBVR), Version 1.5
sources.relevance: Vocabulary and rules for documenting business vocabularies and business rules for exchange; alethic necessity versus deontic obligation, operative/behavioural rules, enforcement level as a graded severity scale, and the business-policy versus business-rule distinction.

sources.title: Decision Model and Notation (DMN), Version 1.5
sources.relevance: Decision requirements, decision logic and decision tables with hit policies (including Priority, First and Collect variants), knowledge sources linking decisions to policy and regulatory authority, and alignment with BPMN process models.

sources.title: NIST SP 800-162, Guide to Attribute Based Access Control (ABAC) Definition and Considerations
sources.organization: National Institute of Standards and Technology (NIST)
sources.relevance: Defines ABAC as evaluation of subject, object, operation and environment attributes against policy, rules or relationships; separates natural-language policy from its machine-processable rendering and locates evaluation in the access decision function rather than the policy statement.

sources.title: PROV-O: The PROV Ontology
sources.relevance: Entity/Activity/Agent with wasDerivedFrom, wasAttributedTo, wasGeneratedBy, wasRevisionOf, hadPrimarySource, generatedAtTime, invalidatedAtTime, specializationOf and alternateOf for the derivation and attribution chain of a statement expression.

sources.title: RFC 3339: Date and Time on the Internet: Timestamps
sources.relevance: Requires seconds in the time component and an explicit offset (Z or plus/minus hh:mm); defines -00:00 for a known UTC instant with unknown local offset; supports string-sortable time ordering.

sources.title: OSCAL Control Catalog Model concepts
sources.organization: National Institute of Standards and Technology (NIST)
sources.version_or_date: NIST OSCAL project documentation, accessed 2 September 2026
sources.relevance: Control, group, part, props, links and back-matter structure; reusable parameters and profile tailoring; metadata with title, version, oscal-version, roles, parties and responsible-party; and the rule that any content change forces a new root uuid and a new last-modified value.

sources.title: European Legislation Identifier (ELI)
sources.organization: Publications Office of the European Union
sources.relevance: Three pillars: flexible URI template for unique human- and machine-readable legislation identifiers, an FRBR-based metadata ontology for exchanging legislation metadata, and RDFa or JSON-LD publication of that metadata.

sources.title: ODRL Formal Semantics (Editor's Draft)
sources.relevance: Documents the evaluator input/output frame (policy, state of the world, evaluation request, evaluation report) and explicitly marks policy-level conflict handling for perm/prohibit/invalid as still unwritten, which is the evidence for recording conflict semantics as a gap rather than a conformance claim.

sources.title: ISO 37301:2021 Compliance management systems - Requirements with guidance for use
sources.relevance: Scope-level requirement to establish, implement, evaluate, maintain and improve a compliance management system, within which compliance obligations are identified, documented and kept current; used here only for obligation-record stewardship and review cadence. Full normative text is paywalled and was not read.

data_elements.name: statement master identifier
data_elements.description: Identifier assigned by the authoritative system of record for the statement.

data_elements.name: statement IRI
data_elements.description: Governed global identifier resolving the abstract statement.

data_elements.name: official title
data_elements.description: Registered title with language tag; may repeat per authentic language.

findings.inline_only_rationale: Identifiers, titles and citation forms are reference values carried directly on the statement record; answering these questions produces no rendered or media-bearing artifact, and the identifier scheme itself is governed by an external registry rather than produced here.

findings.name: Version identity and point-in-time expression
findings.description: Separation of the abstract work from its dated expressions and rendered manifestations, and the identity of each version.

questions.text: How is the abstract statement distinguished from its dated versions and its rendered manifestations?
What version designator is assigned to each expression, and how is version ordering determined?
Which expression is the current consolidated one, and which are historical point-in-time versions?
What must change on the record whenever the content of an expression changes?

data_elements.name: work identifier
data_elements.description: Stable identifier of the abstract statement across all its versions.

data_elements.name: expression version designator
data_elements.description: Version label assigned to a dated expression of the statement.

data_elements.name: expression last-modified instant
data_elements.description: Instant at which the expression record last changed.

artifacts.name: Consolidated point-in-time expression
artifacts.description: A dated, citable rendering of the statement as it stood over a specific interval, produced by consolidating applied modifications.
artifacts.identity_strategy: Authoritative expression identifier from the publishing system of record; otherwise the governed work IRI plus the version designator; otherwise a UUID minted by the adopting Dimension with the fallback reason recorded.

layers.name: Normative classification
layers.description: The force, modality, defeasibility and instrument genre of the statement.

findings.name: Deontic modality, force and defeasibility
findings.description: Which normative modality each rule slot carries, whether it can be violated, how severely, and whether it can be defeated.

questions.text: Which deontic modality does each rule slot carry: obligation, permission, prohibition or right?
Is the statement an alethic necessity that cannot be violated, or a deontic obligation that can be?
What enforcement level on the graded severity scale applies when the statement is violated?
answer_data: ordinal position on the declared scale

questions.text: Is the statement defeasible, and by which declared mechanism may it be defeated?
Does the statement express a strong permission acting as an explicit exception to a prohibition?

data_elements.name: deontic modality code
data_elements.description: Obligation, permission, prohibition or right, asserted per rule slot.

data_elements.name: modality family code
data_elements.description: Alethic or deontic classification of the statement.

data_elements.name: enforcement level code
data_elements.description: Position on the graded severity scale for violation of a behavioural rule.

data_elements.name: defeasibility flag
data_elements.description: Whether the statement admits defeat by a superior or more specific statement.

findings.inline_only_rationale: Modality, enforcement level and defeasibility are coded assertions on the statement record resolved against externally governed vocabularies; the normative text that carries them is held by the authoritative source instrument declared under the provenance layer, so declaring a second artifact here would duplicate it.

findings.name: Instrument genre and binding form
findings.description: What kind of instrument the statement is and how it binds, including whether it is a natural-language original or a derived machine-interpretable rendering.

questions.text: What instrument genre is this statement: legislation, regulation, standard, internal directive, contract or offer?
Does the statement bind unilaterally, or does it require an identified counterparty to be in force?
Is this a natural-language original, a machine-interpretable statement, or a rendering derived from a natural-language original?
Which taxonomy supplies the genre code, and who governs that taxonomy?

data_elements.name: instrument genre code
data_elements.description: Coded genre of the normative instrument.

data_elements.name: binding form code
data_elements.description: Unilateral set, unilateral offer, or bilateral agreement requiring an identified counterparty.

data_elements.name: expression form code
data_elements.description: Natural-language, machine-interpretable, or derived machine rendering.

findings.inline_only_rationale: Genre, binding form and expression form are coded classifications resolved against externally governed taxonomies; the model stores codes and vocabulary references and produces no document of its own for this finding.

bundles.name: Authority and applicability
bundles.description: Who issued the statement, under what mandate, who now owns the record, and over what it claims to apply.
bundles.rationale: LegalRuleML makes Authority and Jurisdiction first-class, XACML carries a PolicyIssuer, ODRL requires an assigner on Offers and Agreements, and OSCAL requires roles, parties and responsible-party assignments; without these a statement cannot be trusted or bounded.

layers.name: Authority and accountability
layers.description: Issuing authority and mandate at origin, and accountable ownership of the record afterwards.

findings.name: Issuing authority and mandate
findings.description: Which party issued the statement, under what legal or organisational competence, and by which recorded adoption decision.

questions.text: Which party issued the statement, and under what legal or organisational mandate?
Which body formally adopted the statement, and by which recorded decision?
Within what competence is the issuing authority empowered to bind?
What evidence supports the authority claim, and where does that evidence record live?

data_elements.name: issuing authority reference
data_elements.description: Reference to the party record of the issuing authority.

data_elements.name: mandate basis reference
data_elements.description: Reference to the enabling instrument conferring authority to issue.

data_elements.name: adoption decision reference
data_elements.description: Reference to the record of the formal adoption or enactment decision.

findings.inline_only_rationale: Authority, mandate and adoption are carried as references to party records and decision records owned by other models; reproducing them here would duplicate externally owned evidence and drift toward owning an approval audit trail that this model explicitly disclaims.

findings.name: Ownership, stewardship and roles
findings.description: Accountable ownership of the statement record after issuance and the roles responsible for review, interpretation and succession.

questions.text: Who is the accountable owner of the statement record after issuance?
Which named roles are responsible for periodic review and for answering interpretation requests?
How are role assignments recorded so that a responsible party can be resolved for any past instant?
What happens to ownership when the issuing authority is reorganised or dissolved?

data_elements.name: record owner reference
data_elements.description: Reference to the accountable owner of the statement record.

data_elements.name: responsible role assignment
data_elements.description: Role identifier, assigned party reference and validity interval.

data_elements.name: owner succession note
data_elements.description: Recorded rule or instrument governing transfer of ownership.

findings.inline_only_rationale: Ownership and role assignments are relationship records pointing at party master data owned elsewhere; they are answered from inline reference fields and time-bounded assignments, with no document produced or required by this model.

layers.name: Applicability scope
layers.description: Where, to whom, to what and under which conditions the statement claims to apply.

findings.name: Jurisdiction and territorial scope
findings.description: The legal or organisational orders and territories over which the statement claims application, and how overlapping claims are declared.

questions.text: Over which jurisdictions or territories does the statement claim application?
Which connecting factor triggers application when a party, resource or activity sits outside the issuing territory?
Which subject-matter competence, as distinct from geography, bounds the statement?
How are overlapping jurisdictional claims from different issuing authorities declared?

data_elements.name: jurisdiction reference
data_elements.description: Reference to the legal or organisational order claimed.

data_elements.name: territorial coverage geometry
data_elements.description: Optional geometry or coded area for territorial application.

data_elements.name: subject-matter competence code
data_elements.description: Coded subject-matter bound on the statement's competence.

findings.inline_only_rationale: Jurisdiction and competence are reference and coded values resolved against externally governed place and legal-order registries; the model records claims and pointers rather than producing any territorial document or map artifact of its own.

findings.name: Subject, target, action and context scope
findings.description: The parties, resources, actions and contextual conditions that bring the statement into application, expressed as references into models that own those things.

questions.text: Which parties, roles or subject attributes fall within the statement's application?
Which resources or object classes are the target of each rule slot?
Which actions or operations does each rule slot govern, and from which action vocabulary?
Which environmental or contextual conditions must hold for the statement to be applicable?
Which processes, systems or datasets declare themselves governed by this statement?

data_elements.name: in-scope party reference
data_elements.description: Reference to a party, role or attribute selector in application scope.

data_elements.name: in-scope target reference
data_elements.description: Reference to a resource or resource collection targeted by a rule slot.

data_elements.name: governed action code
data_elements.description: Coded action governed by a rule slot, drawn from a named action vocabulary.

data_elements.name: applicability context reference
data_elements.description: Reference to a contextual or environmental condition record.

findings.inline_only_rationale: Scope is a set of typed references into party, resource, action-vocabulary and process models that own those entities; materialising them as a local artifact would copy master data this model explicitly places out of scope.

bundles.name: Normative content and composition
bundles.description: The internal structure of the statement, how it composes into and inherits from larger statements, and how it binds to externally owned condition expressions and defined terms.
bundles.rationale: ODRL requires at least one rule and defines atomic rules, inheritFrom and profile conformance; XACML nests PolicySet, Policy and Rule and separates Target from Condition; OSCAL defines reusable parameters and profile tailoring. The condition expression itself is owned by the referenced constraint model.

layers.name: Rule structure and composition
layers.description: Rule-slot inventory, atomicity, containment in policy sets and inheritance from parent statements.

findings.name: Rule-slot inventory and atomicity
findings.description: The complete set of rule slots a statement contains, whether each is atomic, and which duties, remedies or consequences attach to them.

questions.text: What is the complete inventory of rule slots the statement contains, and is each one atomic?
Must the statement contain at least one rule slot to be valid?
answer_data: validity consequence of an empty statement

questions.text: How is a compact statement expanded into atomic rule slots without changing meaning?
Which duties, remedies or consequences attach to a given permission or prohibition slot?

data_elements.name: rule slot
data_elements.description: A single normative slot with modality, action, target and party function.

data_elements.name: rule slot identifier
data_elements.description: Identifier of an individual rule slot within the statement.

data_elements.name: attached duty reference
data_elements.description: Reference to a duty, remedy or consequence attached to a slot.

findings.inline_only_rationale: The rule-slot inventory is the structured body of the statement record itself and is answered entirely from inline structured fields; the rendered form of that body is already covered by the consolidated expression artifact under version identity.

findings.name: Policy-set containment and inheritance
findings.description: How the statement nests inside larger policy sets and inherits rules or properties from parent statements without circularity.

questions.text: Is the statement contained in a larger policy set, and what is the containment path?
From which parent statements does this one inherit rules or properties?
How is circularity in the inheritance graph prevented and detected?
Which parent properties are explicitly not transferred to the child statement?

data_elements.name: containing policy set reference
data_elements.description: Reference to a policy set that contains this statement.

data_elements.name: inherit-from reference
data_elements.description: Reference to a parent statement from which rules or properties are inherited.

data_elements.name: non-inherited property code
data_elements.description: Property explicitly excluded from inheritance.

findings.inline_only_rationale: Containment and inheritance are graph edges between statement records; they are fully answerable from inline reference fields and an acyclicity assertion, and materialising the resolved graph would be a derived view rather than a governed artifact.

layers.name: Condition binding and interpretation
layers.description: References to externally owned condition expressions, the parameter values this subject sets, and the vocabulary that fixes the meaning of terms.

findings.name: Constraint expression binding
findings.description: How each rule slot points at a constraint or rule expression owned by the referenced constraint model, and what binding metadata travels with the pointer.

questions.text: Which externally owned constraint or rule expression does each rule slot bind to?
At which binding point does the expression attach: rule condition, action refinement, or collection refinement?
Which expression language and version is the referenced constraint written in?
What happens to the statement when a referenced expression is unavailable or not understood?

data_elements.name: constraint expression reference
data_elements.description: Pointer to an expression record owned by the referenced constraint model.

data_elements.name: binding point code
data_elements.description: Where the referenced expression attaches within the rule slot.

data_elements.name: unresolved reference handling code
data_elements.description: Declared behaviour when a bound expression cannot be resolved or understood.

findings.inline_only_rationale: This finding deliberately carries only pointers and binding metadata. The constraint expression, its operators, operands and logical composition are owned by WM-KNW-013, so declaring an expression artifact here would reproduce a target model's content and violate the reference boundary.

findings.name: Parameterisation and tailoring values
findings.description: Parameters the statement exposes and the subject-specific values the adopting organisation sets, kept distinct from amendment of the statement itself.

questions.text: Which parameters does the statement expose, and what are their permitted value sets?
Which parameter values has the adopting organisation set for this statement?
Which unit and datatype governs each parameter value?
How is a tailoring change to a parameter distinguished from an amendment of the statement?

data_elements.name: parameter definition
data_elements.description: Declared parameter with identifier, permitted values and default.

data_elements.name: parameter value assignment
data_elements.description: Subject-specific value set by the adopting organisation.

data_elements.name: parameter unit reference
data_elements.description: Unit governing a quantity-valued parameter.

findings.inline_only_rationale: Parameter definitions and assigned values are structured inline data on the statement record; the relation ledger permits this model to carry subject-specific parameters, but producing a tailoring document would encroach on the referenced expression model's own publication surface.

findings.name: Defined terms and vocabulary binding
findings.description: Which governed vocabulary fixes the meaning of terms used in the statement, which terms are defined locally, and which profiles a processor must understand.

questions.text: Which controlled vocabulary supplies the meaning of terms used in the statement?
Which locally defined terms override an otherwise applicable general definition, and within what scope?
Which profile identifiers must a consuming processor understand before interpreting the statement?
How are term definitions versioned relative to the statement that uses them?

data_elements.name: vocabulary reference
data_elements.description: Reference to a governed vocabulary or concept scheme.

data_elements.name: local term definition
data_elements.description: Term defined within the statement, with its scope of application.

data_elements.name: required profile identifier
data_elements.description: Profile a processor must understand to interpret the statement.

artifacts.name: Governed vocabulary or glossary
artifacts.description: The controlled vocabulary, glossary or concept scheme that fixes the meaning of terms used in the statement, referenced at a pinned version.
artifacts.identity_strategy: Authoritative vocabulary identifier from the registry that manages the vocabulary; otherwise the governed vocabulary IRI plus version token; otherwise a UUID minted by the adopting Dimension for a locally held glossary.

bundles.name: Precedence, conflict and exceptions
bundles.description: How the statement declares its precedence relative to other statements, how conflicts are named, and which derogations and open interpretations are on record.
bundles.rationale: The known-relation ledger explicitly keeps generic conflict rules in this model. XACML combining algorithm identifiers, DMN hit policies, ODRL conflict terms and LegalRuleML Override relations are declarations carried by the statement; their execution belongs to a referenced runtime.

layers.name: Precedence and conflict declaration
layers.description: Declared strategy identifiers and pairwise superiority relations that determine which statement prevails.

findings.name: Combining and hit-policy declaration
findings.description: The strategy identifier the statement declares for reconciling multiple applicable rule slots, and where the normative definition of that strategy lives.

questions.text: Which combining or hit-policy strategy identifier does the statement declare for its rule slots?
Where is the normative definition of that strategy published, and who owns its execution?
Is the declared strategy order-sensitive, and if so what fixes the order?
Which conflict term applies when a permission and a prohibition both match?

data_elements.name: combining strategy identifier
data_elements.description: Declared identifier of the combining or hit-policy strategy.

data_elements.name: strategy definition reference
data_elements.description: Pointer to the specification defining the declared strategy.

data_elements.name: conflict term code
data_elements.description: Declared policy-level conflict resolution term.

findings.inline_only_rationale: These are coded declarations pointing at strategies defined in external specifications. The evaluation that applies a combining algorithm or hit policy belongs to a referenced decision runtime, so this model produces no artifact and asserts no execution semantics here.

findings.name: Override and superiority relations
findings.description: Pairwise precedence between this statement and others, the ground on which precedence rests, and what is recorded when nothing resolves a conflict.

questions.text: Which other statements does this one override, and which override it?
On what declared ground does an override rest, such as specificity, recency or hierarchy of authority?
Is the resulting precedence graph acyclic, and how is that checked?
What is recorded when a conflict is detected but no superiority relation resolves it?

data_elements.name: overrides reference
data_elements.description: Statement over which this one takes precedence.

data_elements.name: overridden-by reference
data_elements.description: Statement that takes precedence over this one.

data_elements.name: override ground code
data_elements.description: Declared basis for the superiority relation.

data_elements.name: unresolved conflict record
data_elements.description: Record naming a detected but unresolved conflict and its escalation route.

findings.inline_only_rationale: Superiority relations are typed edges between statement records with a declared ground; they are answered from inline reference fields, and the model records rather than resolves conflicts, so no adjudication document is produced.

layers.name: Exceptions and open interpretations
layers.description: Registered derogations from the statement and formally recorded competing readings of it.

findings.name: Derogation and waiver declaration
findings.description: Registered exceptions, waivers and derogations from the statement, their granting authority, scope, period and compensating obligations.

questions.text: Which exceptions, waivers or derogations from this statement are currently registered?
Which authority may grant a derogation, and is that authority distinct from the issuer?
For which parties, resources or period does each derogation hold?
Which compensating obligation or remedy attaches to a granted derogation?

data_elements.name: derogation record reference
data_elements.description: Reference to a registered derogation, waiver or exception.

data_elements.name: granting authority reference
data_elements.description: Party empowered to grant the derogation.

data_elements.name: derogation validity interval
data_elements.description: Start and end instants over which the derogation holds.

data_elements.name: compensating obligation reference
data_elements.description: Obligation attached as a condition of the derogation.

artifacts.name: Granted derogation or waiver instrument
artifacts.description: The instrument by which a competent authority grants a time-bounded exception from named rule slots, with its scope and any compensating obligations.
artifacts.identity_strategy: Authoritative derogation register number issued by the granting authority's system of record; otherwise a governed IRI minted for the derogation; otherwise a ULID minted by the adopting Dimension with the fallback reason recorded.

findings.name: Declared conflicts and alternative interpretations
findings.description: Competing readings, known contradictions and semantic gaps recorded against the statement so that consumers are not misled into assuming settled meaning.

questions.text: Which competing interpretations of the statement are formally recorded as alternatives?
Which contradictions with other statements are identified but not yet resolved?
Which parts of the applicable standard's semantics are non-normative or incomplete for this statement?
Who decides between recorded alternatives, and how is that decision captured?

data_elements.name: alternative interpretation record
data_elements.description: A recorded competing reading with its proposer and status.

data_elements.name: known contradiction note
data_elements.description: Narrative record of an unresolved contradiction with another statement.

data_elements.name: semantic gap note
data_elements.description: Recorded incompleteness in an aligned standard's semantics.

findings.inline_only_rationale: Alternatives, contradictions and semantic gaps are narrative and reference annotations attached to the statement record; they are consumed as inline caveats and would lose their binding to the specific rule slot if separated into a standalone document.

bundles.name: Lifecycle, time and provenance
bundles.description: How the statement record moves through its states, over which intervals it is in force and efficacious, and where its content came from.
bundles.rationale: Akoma Ntoso and LegalRuleML separate in-force, efficacy and applicability and require dated lifecycle events; PROV-O supplies the derivation and attribution chain; RFC 3339 fixes the timestamp form and the separation of event time from record time.

layers.name: Lifecycle and supersession
layers.description: Permitted states of the statement record and the amendment, replacement and repeal relations between statements.

findings.name: Statement lifecycle state model
findings.description: The permitted lifecycle states of the statement record, the transitions between them, and which transitions depend on an external approval decision.

questions.text: What are the permitted lifecycle states of the statement record, from draft to repealed?
Which transitions are permitted, and which require an external approval decision?
How is suspension recorded, and what does it change about applicability while it lasts?
Which lifecycle events must carry a date, and which are merely recorded?

data_elements.name: lifecycle state code
data_elements.description: Current state of the statement record.

data_elements.name: permitted transition
data_elements.description: Allowed from-state to to-state pair with any approval requirement.

data_elements.name: suspension record
data_elements.description: Recorded suspension with its interval and granting authority.

findings.inline_only_rationale: Lifecycle states and transitions are structured state data on the statement record. The approval decisions that authorise transitions live in decision records owned elsewhere, and this model references them rather than reproducing an approval dossier.

findings.name: Amendment, supersession and repeal
findings.description: Which statements this one amends, replaces or repeals, at what provision granularity, and what a processor must do when replacement is declared.

questions.text: Which statements does this one amend, replace or repeal, and at which provision granularity?
Which amending instrument produced the current consolidated expression?
What must a processor do when the statement declares that it has been replaced?
How is a partial repeal distinguished from a full repeal in the record?

data_elements.name: amends reference
data_elements.description: Statement amended, replaced or repealed by this one.

data_elements.name: replaced-by reference
data_elements.description: Statement that replaces this one.

data_elements.name: modification type code
data_elements.description: Amendment, partial repeal, full repeal or consolidation.

data_elements.name: affected provision anchor
data_elements.description: Pointer to the specific provision changed by a modification.

artifacts.name: Amending or repealing instrument
artifacts.description: The instrument that changes or removes provisions of a statement, carrying the modification set and the provisions it affects.
artifacts.identity_strategy: Authoritative instrument identifier issued by the enacting or publishing system of record; otherwise the governed instrument IRI; otherwise a UUID minted by the adopting Dimension with the fallback reason recorded.

layers.name: Temporal validity
layers.description: The intervals over which the statement is in force, efficacious and applicable, and the separation of event time from record time.

findings.name: Validity intervals and record time
findings.description: Distinct in-force, efficacy and applicability intervals, expressed as RFC 3339 instants, with event time kept separate from observation or ingestion time.

questions.text: When does the statement enter into force, and is that distinct from when it was adopted?
Over which interval is the statement efficacious, and can efficacy begin after entry into force?
To which facts or periods does the statement apply, as distinct from when it is in force?
What is the observation or ingestion instant at which each dated occurrence was captured in the register?
How is an instant with an unknown local offset represented without falsely asserting UTC local time?

data_elements.name: entry-into-force instant
data_elements.description: RFC 3339 instant at which the statement enters into force.

data_elements.name: efficacy interval
data_elements.description: Start and end instants over which the statement is efficacious.

data_elements.name: applicability interval
data_elements.description: Period of facts to which the statement applies, which may precede entry into force.

data_elements.name: record ingestion time
data_elements.description: Instant at which the register captured the occurrence, distinct from event time.

findings.inline_only_rationale: Validity intervals and timestamps are scalar and interval values on the statement record; they are consumed by point-in-time resolution and carry no rendered form, so no artifact is declared and none is required to answer the questions.

layers.name: Provenance and source mapping
layers.description: Where the statement's content came from, who is accountable for it, and which authoritative provision each rule slot derives from.

findings.name: Authoring, derivation and source mapping
findings.description: The attribution and derivation chain of the expression, and the mapping from rule slots to authoritative source provisions including fidelity of any machine rendering.

questions.text: Which agents authored, revised or are otherwise accountable for the expression's content?
From which prior entity was this expression derived, and by which activity?
Which authoritative source provision does each rule slot derive from?
Is the machine-interpretable statement a faithful rendering of a natural-language original, and who certified that?
Which primary source is cited, as distinct from an intermediate compilation or consolidation?

data_elements.name: attributed agent reference
data_elements.description: Agent to whom the expression or a revision is attributed.

data_elements.name: derived-from reference
data_elements.description: Prior entity from which the expression was derived.

data_elements.name: provision anchor
data_elements.description: Pointer to a specific provision of an authoritative source text.

data_elements.name: rendering fidelity attestation
data_elements.description: Reference to an attestation that a machine rendering is faithful to its natural-language original.

data_elements.name: expression generation instant
data_elements.description: Instant at which the expression was generated.

artifacts.name: Authoritative source instrument
artifacts.description: The published instrument that is the primary source of the statement's normative content, cited at provision granularity.
media_or_form: published standard or code of practice
artifacts.identity_strategy: Authoritative publication identifier assigned by the official publisher's system of record; otherwise the governed legislation or standard identifier IRI; otherwise a UUID minted by the adopting Dimension with the fallback reason recorded.

bundles.name: Assurance, disclosure and interoperability
bundles.description: Declared alignments and structural conformance of the statement, its review status, and how the record itself is classified, disclosed and retained.
bundles.rationale: Standards must be recorded as alignments rather than conformance claims; OSCAL fixes manifestation integrity and metadata change rules; ISO 37301 requires compliance obligations to be documented and kept current; Akoma Ntoso and ELI govern publication and point-in-time retrievability.

layers.name: Assurance and alignment
layers.description: Review status and recorded defects of the statement, and its declared structural conformance and standard alignments.

findings.name: Statement quality and review status
findings.description: Review cadence, recorded defects in the statement itself, and confidence in any machine-interpretable rendering.

questions.text: When was the statement last reviewed, and when is the next review due?
Which recorded defects affect the statement, such as ambiguity, unreachable rule slots or missing definitions?
What is the declared confidence in the machine-interpretable rendering of the statement?
Which review outcomes require the statement to be withdrawn from use?

data_elements.name: last review instant
data_elements.description: Instant of the most recent recorded review.

data_elements.name: next review due instant
data_elements.description: Instant by which the next review must occur.

data_elements.name: recorded defect
data_elements.description: Defect recorded against the statement with type, severity and affected slot.

findings.inline_only_rationale: Review status and defect records are governance metadata held inline on the statement record; the review meetings, findings dossiers and assessment reports that produce them belong to a compliance-management model that this model deliberately does not own.

findings.name: Structural conformance and standard alignment
findings.description: Which external standards or profiles the statement declares alignment with, which structural requirements make it well-formed, and how published manifestations are integrity-checked.

questions.text: Which external standards or profiles does the statement declare alignment with, and on what evidence?
Which structural requirements must hold for the statement to be well-formed, independent of any runtime?
Which declared alignments are partial, and where do the semantics diverge?
Which serialization bindings are published, and how is manifestation integrity verified?

data_elements.name: alignment declaration
data_elements.description: Declared alignment to an external standard with its evidence and scope.

data_elements.name: well-formedness rule reference
data_elements.description: Reference to the structural rule set the statement must satisfy.

data_elements.name: alignment divergence note
data_elements.description: Recorded semantic divergence in a partial alignment.

data_elements.name: manifestation integrity digest
data_elements.description: Content digest binding a published manifestation to its expression.

artifacts.name: Machine-readable statement manifestation
artifacts.description: A published serialization of one expression of the statement, paired with a content digest and the identifier of the expression it manifests.
artifacts.identity_strategy: Authoritative manifestation identifier from the publishing system of record; otherwise the governed expression IRI combined with a format token; otherwise a UUID minted by the adopting Dimension, in all cases paired with a content digest.

layers.name: Disclosure and retention
layers.description: Sensitivity classification and publication audience of the statement record, and retention and disposition of superseded expressions.

findings.name: Record classification, access and retention
findings.description: How the statement record itself is classified and published, and how long its superseded expressions are retained before a declared disposition.

questions.text: What sensitivity classification applies to the statement record itself, as distinct from what it governs?
Which statements are published openly, and which are restricted to named audiences?
Which parts of a statement may be redacted while leaving it citable?
How long must superseded expressions be retained to support point-in-time reconstruction?
Which disposition action applies at the end of retention, who executes it, and what tombstone remains resolvable?

data_elements.name: record classification code
data_elements.description: Sensitivity classification of the statement record.

data_elements.name: publication audience code
data_elements.description: Declared audience for the published expression.

data_elements.name: retention period
data_elements.description: Minimum period for which superseded expressions must be retained.

data_elements.name: disposition action code
data_elements.description: Destruction, transfer or permanent preservation at end of retention.

data_elements.name: tombstone record
data_elements.description: Minimal resolvable record left after disposition of an expression.

findings.inline_only_rationale: Classification, audience, retention period, disposition class and tombstone are declarative fields on the statement record. Execution of destruction, transfer or preservation, and the log of that execution, belong to the adopting Dimension's records-retention authority, so no artifact is produced here.

functions.name: Register a normative statement
functions.description: Create a governed record for a normative statement with an identifier, an issuing authority, an instrument genre and at least one rule slot.
outputs: assigned master identifier or minted fallback identifier
preconditions: An issuing authority reference resolves in the party model
At least one rule slot with a deontic modality and a governed action is supplied
The identity priority has been applied and any fallback reason recorded
effects: Statement identifier is reserved and made resolvable
Adoption event time and register ingestion time are recorded separately
Provenance attribution for the initial expression is recorded

functions.name: Issue a new version expression
functions.description: Create a new dated expression of an existing statement work and link it to the expression it supersedes.
outputs: new expression record with version designator
new record UUID and last-modified instant
