bundles.name: Address record and structure
bundles.description: What an address is as a governed record: its identifier, the specification and class it instantiates, the components that scope it, the locators that pinpoint it, and its aliases and rendered representations.
bundles.rationale: ISO 19160-1 treats the address as a modelled class with mandatory identity, lifecycle and metadata, and exists to allow cross-mapping between address specifications; INSPIRE realises that as a concrete schema with Address, AddressComponent subtypes and AddressLocator. Structure must therefore be modelled before any use of an address.

layers.name: Address identity and classification
layers.description: Identifiers that make an address referable and de-duplicable, and the class and specification profile that determine which structure is legal for it.

findings.name: Address identifier and uniqueness scope
findings.description: The identifier or identifiers that designate the address record itself, distinct from the identifier of the object addressed or of any position, together with the scope in which uniqueness holds and the change events that force a new identifier.

questions.text: Which authoritative master-system identifier designates this address, and which register issued it?
Does the address carry a governed global identifier or resolvable IRI in addition to the local register key, and is it persistent?
Which alternative, legacy or third-party identifiers are recorded, and to which system is each scoped?
Under which changes does the identifier stay stable, and which change compels minting a new one?
Within what scope is uniqueness enforced — single register, jurisdiction, country or globally?

data_elements.name: Address identifier
data_elements.description: Primary identifier of the address record, issued by the addressing authority's register; mandatory wherever the record claims lifecycle conformance.

data_elements.name: Identifier scheme
data_elements.description: Namespace or scheme under which the identifier is issued, allowing two identifiers from different registers to be told apart.

data_elements.name: Governed global identifier
data_elements.description: Stable HTTP URI or other governed global identifier for the address as a spatial thing.

data_elements.name: Alternative identifier
data_elements.description: External or legacy identifier for the same address, each qualified by its owning system.

data_elements.name: Identifier stability rule
data_elements.description: Declared rule stating which changes preserve and which changes break identifier continuity.

artifacts.name: Address register entry
artifacts.description: The authoritative record for one address held by the issuing register, carrying the identifier, components, locators, status and position; the unit that a resolvable identifier dereferences to.
artifacts.identity_strategy: Register key issued by the addressing authority, optionally expressed as a persistent HTTP URI when the register publishes resolvable identifiers.

findings.name: Address class and governing specification profile
findings.description: The class of address the record instantiates and the national or community address specification that fixes which components are legal, mandatory or forbidden for that class.

questions.text: Which address class does this record instantiate — numbered thoroughfare, landmark, postal delivery, or another declared class?
Which address specification or class profile governs this record, and at which version?
Does the record designate a location, a point of postal delivery, or both, and how is that role encoded?
answer_data: Consumers permitted to rely on each role

questions.text: How does this class map to the corresponding classes of each standard the register claims alignment with?

data_elements.name: Address class
data_elements.description: Classification of the address into a declared class such as numbered thoroughfare, landmark or postal delivery address.

data_elements.name: Governing address specification
data_elements.description: Reference to the address specification or class profile that constrains the record's structure.

data_elements.name: Address role
data_elements.description: Whether the record designates a physical location, a delivery point, or both; postal delivery addresses may bear no definite relation to the recipient's location.

data_elements.name: Profile version
data_elements.description: Version identifier of the governing specification at the time the record was validated.

artifacts.name: Address specification / class profile
artifacts.description: The document or machine-readable profile that declares the address classes recognised in a jurisdiction and the components permitted, required or prohibited for each.
artifacts.identity_strategy: Specification identifier plus semantic version; each published edition carries an RFC 3339 issue timestamp.

layers.name: Address composition and locators
layers.description: The internal parts of an address: scoping components in their hierarchy, locator designators and sub-address levels, and alias or rendered representations.

findings.name: Address components and their hierarchy
findings.description: The administrative, address-area, postal and thoroughfare components that scope an address, the level at which each sits, and whether each is a reference to an authoritative feature or free text.

questions.text: Which components scope this address, and what level does each occupy in the hierarchy?
answer_data: Component type (admin unit, address area, postal descriptor, thoroughfare)

questions.text: Which components are mandatory, conditional or prohibited for this class in this country?
Does each component reference an authoritative external feature, or repeat a name as unlinked text?
How are sub-country administrative levels ordered and labelled, and how does that ordering survive exchange?

data_elements.name: Address component
data_elements.description: A component that defines the scope of the address: administrative unit name, address area name, postal descriptor or thoroughfare name.

data_elements.name: Component type
data_elements.description: Which kind of address component the entry is, drawn from the governing specification's component vocabulary.

data_elements.name: Administrative level index
data_elements.description: Ordinal position of an administrative component in the hierarchy, descending in generality.

data_elements.name: Component obligation
data_elements.description: Whether the component is mandatory, conditional or prohibited for the address class in the applicable territory.

findings.inline_only_rationale: Components are structural parts of the address record: they are carried either inline as names or as references to features owned by sibling models, and produce no separate document. The document that fixes their obligations is the address specification profile already held in the address-classification finding.

findings.name: Locator designators and sub-addressing
findings.description: The human-readable designators and names that distinguish the addressable object within its component scope, including house numbers with non-numeric parts and the building, floor, unit, room and seat levels beneath them.

questions.text: Which locator designators identify the object within its scope, and at which locator level does each apply?
answer_data: Component the locator is within the scope of

questions.text: Is the house number a plain ordinal, a range, a hyphenated compound or a non-numeric token, and how is it normalised for sorting and matching?
Which sub-address levels are addressable in their own right, and which are descriptive only?
When a sub-address exists, does it reference a parent address record or stand alone, and what breaks if the parent is retired?

data_elements.name: Locator designator
data_elements.description: Numbers, characters or codes that distinguish the addressable object within its scope, such as a house number and its suffix.

data_elements.name: Locator designator type
data_elements.description: Type of the designator, for example address number, building name, unit designator, floor or room.

data_elements.name: Locator level
data_elements.description: Level at which the locator applies — site, access, unit or postal delivery point.

data_elements.name: Locator name
data_elements.description: Proper name identifying the addressable object, such as a building or estate name, used alongside or instead of a number.

data_elements.name: Parent address
data_elements.description: Reference to the parent address that a sub-address is derived from.

artifacts.name: Sub-address designator vocabulary
artifacts.description: The controlled list of secondary unit and sub-address designators (apartment, suite, floor, building, room, seat) with approved abbreviations for a territory.
artifacts.identity_strategy: Publisher identifier plus publication edition; USPS Publication 28 dated October 2024 is one such edition.

findings.name: Address aliases and rendered representations
findings.description: Alias relations between address records and the language-, script- and purpose-specific rendered forms of the same address, including which form is authoritative for which use.

questions.text: Which address records are aliases of which primary address, and what is the alias relation type?
answer_data: Period during which the alias is honoured

questions.text: Which rendered or transliterated representations exist, and in which language and script is each written?
Which representation is authoritative for legal service of documents, and which for mail delivery?
May an alias be used as a matching key, and with what confidence penalty?
answer_data: Audit requirement when an alias resolves a match

data_elements.name: Alias of
data_elements.description: Reference from an alias record to the primary address it stands for.

data_elements.name: Alias type
data_elements.description: Nature of the alias: vanity address, historic form, postal variant, transliteration or common usage.

data_elements.name: Rendered representation
data_elements.description: A complete rendered form of the address as a string or ordered lines, qualified by language and script.

data_elements.name: Representation language and script
data_elements.description: Language tag and script of the rendered form; the UPU notes at least twenty scripts in official addressing use.

data_elements.name: Authoritative purpose
data_elements.description: The purpose for which a given representation is the authoritative one, such as legal service, emergency dispatch or delivery.

findings.inline_only_rationale: Aliases and rendered representations are relational and derived data held inside the address register: an alias is a typed link between two register entries, and a rendering is produced on demand by applying a template. The template itself is an artifact and is held in the postal rendering finding rather than duplicated here.

bundles.name: Assignment authority, lifecycle and object binding
bundles.description: Who may create, change and retire an address, under which numbering rules, through which lifecycle states and temporal versions, and to which object in a sibling model the address is bound.
bundles.rationale: FGDC-STD-016-2011 places Address Authority among lineage attributes and defines Address Lifecycle Status and Address Anomaly Status relative to a governing Address Reference System; ISO 19160-1 makes lifecycle attributes mandatory for lifecycle-conformant classes; INSPIRE separates real-world validity from record version lifespan. Authority, rules, states and binding are therefore not optional metadata but the core of a trustworthy reference.

layers.name: Addressing authority and numbering rules
layers.description: The mandated body, its jurisdiction, and the address reference system whose numbering scheme determines whether a candidate address is well formed.

findings.name: Addressing authority, mandate and jurisdiction
findings.description: The body legally empowered to assign, alter and retire addresses in a territory, the instrument granting that power, the extent within which it applies, and how non-authoritative address creation is handled.

questions.text: Which body holds the mandate to assign, alter and retire addresses here, and under what legal instrument?
Who stewards the address record, as distinct from whoever owns the object addressed?
What is the geographic extent of the authority's jurisdiction, and how are overlaps or gaps at its boundary resolved?
What status is given to an address created by a developer, occupier or crowd source rather than the authority?

data_elements.name: Address authority
data_elements.description: The address authority responsible for the address, recorded as a lineage attribute of the record.

data_elements.name: Mandate instrument
data_elements.description: Reference to the statute, by-law or delegation that grants addressing power.

data_elements.name: Jurisdiction extent
data_elements.description: Territory within which the authority may assign addresses, as a geometry or an administrative unit reference.

data_elements.name: Authority effective period
data_elements.description: Period during which the mandate was in force, so historic records can be judged against the authority of their time.

artifacts.name: Addressing mandate instrument
artifacts.description: The statute, ordinance, by-law or delegation document that designates an addressing authority and delimits its jurisdiction and powers.
artifacts.identity_strategy: Official instrument number issued by the enacting body, with commencement date recorded as an RFC 3339 timestamp; a date alone is never the identifier.

findings.name: Address reference system and numbering rules
findings.description: The numbering scheme governing an area — axis origin and direction, block ranges, intervals, parity and reservation rules — and the tests that decide whether a candidate address conforms to it.

questions.text: Which numbering scheme governs this address, including axis origin, direction, interval, parity and block ranges?
What test determines that a candidate number is valid within the governing reference system?
answer_data: Anomaly status when the test fails

questions.text: How are numbers reserved, skipped or reissued when a parcel is subdivided or consolidated?
Where two schemes overlap the same ground, which one governs, and who decides?

data_elements.name: Address reference system identifier
data_elements.description: Identifier of the numbering scheme that governs addresses in an area.

data_elements.name: Numbering axis and origin
data_elements.description: Description of the axis, origin and direction along which numbers increase.

data_elements.name: Permitted number range
data_elements.description: Low and high bounds permitted for a block or segment under the scheme.

data_elements.name: Parity rule
data_elements.description: Rule assigning odd and even numbers to sides of a thoroughfare.

artifacts.name: Address reference system definition
artifacts.description: The published definition of a numbering scheme: grid or axis description, range tables, parity conventions and the map or geometry delimiting where the scheme applies.
artifacts.identity_strategy: Reference system identifier assigned by the addressing authority, versioned on each amendment with an RFC 3339 effective timestamp.

layers.name: Lifecycle state and temporal versioning
layers.description: Lifecycle status and its permitted transitions, and the separate axes of real-world validity and record version lifespan.

findings.name: Lifecycle status and permitted transitions
findings.description: The current lifecycle status of an address, the transition and evidence that produced it, the distinction between official status and lifecycle status, and how long a retired address remains resolvable.

questions.text: What is the current lifecycle status of the address, and which transition produced it?
Which transitions are permitted, who may authorise each, and what evidence must accompany them?
Is a retired address retained for historical resolution, and for how long does it stay resolvable?
May an address be reserved or proposed before the object exists, and what obligations follow from that state?
answer_data: Obligations and expiry of the reservation
Consumers permitted to use a pre-active address

questions.text: How does official status differ from lifecycle status in this register, and can a record be active but unofficial?

data_elements.name: Address lifecycle status
data_elements.description: Lifecycle status of the address, typically potential, proposed, active or retired.

data_elements.name: Official status
data_elements.description: Whether the address is officially recognised by the authority, independent of whether it is in current use.

data_elements.name: Status change time
data_elements.description: Time at which the current status took effect, as an RFC 3339 timestamp with an explicit offset or Z.

data_elements.name: Superseding address
data_elements.description: Reference to the address that replaces a retired record, enabling historic resolution to a current one.

artifacts.name: Address assignment or retirement decision record
artifacts.description: The authority's decision that creates, changes or retires an address, recording the basis, the affected object, the resulting status and the approving officer.
artifacts.identity_strategy: Decision or case number issued by the addressing authority; decision timestamps are RFC 3339 and never substitute for the number.

findings.name: Real-world validity versus record version lifespan
findings.description: The two distinct time axes an address carries — the period the address is valid in the real world, and the period a particular version of the record was current in the register — together with observation and ingestion times and the separation of corrections from real change.

questions.text: When did the address become valid in the real world, and when did it cease to be valid?
When did this version of the record begin and end in the register, independent of real-world validity?
Are all recorded times expressed per RFC 3339 with seconds and an explicit offset or Z, and how is an unknown local offset represented?
answer_data: Offset handling rule including -00:00 for unknown offset

questions.text: How is a correction to a past record distinguished from a real-world change, and does a correction alter the validity period?
answer_data: Effect on validity versus version period

questions.text: What is the observation or ingestion time of this version, and does it differ from the event time it reports?

data_elements.name: Valid from
data_elements.description: Time when the address started, or is planned to start, being used in the real world.

data_elements.name: Valid to
data_elements.description: Time when the address ceased, or is expected to cease, being used in the real world.

data_elements.name: Version begin
data_elements.description: Time at which this version of the record was inserted into the register.

data_elements.name: Version end
data_elements.description: Time at which this version of the record was superseded or removed from the register.

data_elements.name: Observation or ingestion time
data_elements.description: Time at which the asserting party observed or ingested the fact, kept separate from the event time it describes.

data_elements.name: Change kind
data_elements.description: Whether a new version records a real-world change, a correction of an error, or an enrichment from a new source.

artifacts.name: Address register change log
artifacts.description: The ordered history of record versions for an address or register, from which any past state can be reconstructed and corrections told apart from real-world change.
artifacts.identity_strategy: Register identifier plus monotonically increasing version or sequence number; each entry timestamped in RFC 3339 with an explicit offset or Z.

layers.name: Binding to the addressable object
layers.description: How an address attaches, as a mixin, to an object owned by a sibling model, and what governs that attachment.

findings.name: Address-to-object binding and its basis
findings.description: The act that binds an address to an addressable object in another model, its evidential basis, its cardinality in both directions, its exclusivity per purpose, and what happens when the object is demolished, merged or subdivided.

questions.text: Which addressable object does this address designate, in which sibling model, and by which identifier?
Can one object hold several addresses and one address designate several objects, and which combinations are legal here?
What basis justified the binding — building permit, survey, occupancy certificate or field observation?
What happens to the address when the object is demolished, merged or subdivided?
Is the binding exclusive for legal service, emergency dispatch and delivery alike, or may these differ?

data_elements.name: Addressable object
data_elements.description: Reference to the object the address designates, held in a sibling model such as building, parcel or spatial unit.

data_elements.name: Owning model
data_elements.description: Identifier of the sibling model that defines the referenced object, so the reference can be resolved without guessing.

data_elements.name: Binding basis
data_elements.description: Evidential basis on which the address was bound to the object.

data_elements.name: Binding effective from
data_elements.description: RFC 3339 timestamp from which the binding takes effect.

data_elements.name: Binding purpose
data_elements.description: The purpose for which this binding is authoritative, such as legal service, emergency response or delivery.

artifacts.name: Address binding record
artifacts.description: The record of the act that attaches an address to an addressable object, carrying object reference, basis, purpose and effective period; the concrete form the mixin takes when applied to a host subject.
artifacts.identity_strategy: Composite of address identifier and object identifier plus effective-from timestamp, or a register-issued binding key where the authority issues one.

bundles.name: Thoroughfares and postal designation
bundles.description: Named ways used in addressing and their continuity across renaming, and the postal descriptors, delivery point types and templates that turn a stored address into a deliverable one.
bundles.rationale: INSPIRE models ThoroughfareName as an address component associated with a transport link, RFC 5139 decomposes road elements into named parts, and ISO 19160-4 with UPU S42 governs postal components and rendering templates. Naming and postal rendering are distinct concerns from address identity and are governed by different bodies.

layers.name: Thoroughfare identity, naming and continuity
layers.description: Official names of streets, roads and waterways used for addressing, their decomposition into parts, and their behaviour under renaming, splitting and merging.

findings.name: Thoroughfare identity and name decomposition
findings.description: The identifier of a thoroughfare independent of its current name, the decomposition of a complete street name into directional, type, modifier and base parts, its addressing-relevant extent, and the kinds of way admissible for addressing.

questions.text: Which identifier designates the thoroughfare independently of whatever name it currently bears?
How is the complete street name decomposed into pre-directional, pre-type, pre-modifier, base name, post-type, post-directional and post-modifier parts?
What is the addressing extent of the thoroughfare, and how does it link to the transport network feature that carries its geometry?
Which kinds of way are admissible as addressing thoroughfares in this jurisdiction, and which are excluded?

data_elements.name: Thoroughfare identifier
data_elements.description: Identifier of the thoroughfare as an addressing component, stable across name changes.

data_elements.name: Complete street name
data_elements.description: The full official name as written, from which parts are derived.

data_elements.name: Street name part
data_elements.description: An individual part of the name with its part type, such as pre-directional, street type or post-modifier.

data_elements.name: Thoroughfare kind
data_elements.description: Kind of way — road, street, path, waterway or other passage used for addressing.

data_elements.name: Transport link
data_elements.description: Reference to the transport network feature whose geometry and topology the transport model owns.

artifacts.name: Official street name register entry
artifacts.description: The authority's record of an officially named thoroughfare, carrying identifier, name forms, kind, extent and approval reference.
artifacts.identity_strategy: Thoroughfare identifier issued by the naming authority; names are versioned attributes of that identifier, never identifiers themselves.

findings.name: Renaming, splitting and name continuity
findings.description: How renaming, splitting and merging events are recorded, how long superseded names remain usable for delivery, dispatch and legal documents, and what happens to the addresses on the affected way.

questions.text: What renaming, splitting or merging events has this thoroughfare undergone, and when did each take effect?
For how long do superseded names remain acceptable for delivery, emergency dispatch and legal documents, and do those periods differ?
How are the addresses on the thoroughfare preserved or reissued across the change?
answer_data: Reissue or preserve decision per address

questions.text: Which body approves a renaming, what consultation is required, and where is the decision recorded?

data_elements.name: Name change event
data_elements.description: A renaming, splitting or merging event affecting the thoroughfare, with kind and effective time.

data_elements.name: Previous name
data_elements.description: A superseded name form retained for historical resolution and legacy matching.

data_elements.name: Name validity period
data_elements.description: Period during which a given name form was official, expressed with RFC 3339 timestamps.

data_elements.name: Acceptance grace period
data_elements.description: Duration for which a superseded name is still accepted for a stated purpose.

findings.inline_only_rationale: Renaming continuity is expressed as versioned name attributes and typed event links inside the street name register; the approving instrument is captured by the addressing mandate artifact and the register change log, so a separate artifact here would duplicate them.

layers.name: Postal designation, delivery points and rendering
layers.description: Postcodes and post names, delivery point types, and the country templates and rules that render stored components into a deliverable address.

findings.name: Postal descriptor and delivery point type
findings.description: The postcode and post name that route mail, the operator that maintains them, whether the descriptor bears an authoritative extent, whether the postal city may differ from the municipality, and which kind of delivery point is designated.

questions.text: What postcode and post name apply, and which designated postal operator maintains them?
Is this a physical delivery point, a post office box, poste restante, a rural or highway contract route, or a military address?
Does the postal descriptor have a geographic extent, and is that extent authoritative or an approximation derived from delivery points?
May the postal city name differ from the municipality of location, and which is authoritative for which purpose?
How often does the operator revise postal codes, and how are revisions propagated to bound addresses?
answer_data: Release cadence and latest release identifier

data_elements.name: Postcode
data_elements.description: Code created and maintained for postal purposes to identify a subdivision of addresses and delivery points.

data_elements.name: Post name
data_elements.description: Name created and maintained for postal purposes to identify a subdivision of addresses and delivery points.

data_elements.name: Postal operator
data_elements.description: Designated operator responsible for the postal descriptors used.

data_elements.name: Delivery point type
data_elements.description: Kind of delivery point: physical address, post office box, rural or highway contract route, general delivery or military address.

data_elements.name: Postal city
data_elements.description: Alternate city name used for mailing when it differs from the actual locality of the address.

artifacts.name: Postal code and delivery point reference dataset
artifacts.description: The operator-maintained reference data used to validate, cleanse and standardise addresses, released as dated versions covering a territory.
artifacts.identity_strategy: Publisher plus release identifier and release date, for example a universal postcode database release such as 2026.1 dated 2026-03-02.

findings.name: Postal address template and rendering rules
findings.description: The country-specific template and rendering rules that select, order, concatenate and format components into output lines, the contextual parameters that vary the result, and the handling of components with no target in the destination template.

questions.text: Which country template governs rendering for this destination, at which version, and where is it obtained?
What line identification, ordering, concatenation and formatting rules apply, and which components are optional in each line?
Which contextual parameters change the rendering, such as origin country, domestic versus international, or script?
answer_data: Default when a parameter is absent

questions.text: How are addressee and organisation segments kept separate from the location components this model owns?
answer_data: Party model reference for addressee data

questions.text: What is done when a stored component has no mapping in the destination template?

data_elements.name: Postal address template
data_elements.description: Reference to the country template expressing rendering rules for the destination.

data_elements.name: Template language
data_elements.description: The formal language in which the template is expressed for computer processing.

data_elements.name: Rendered output line
data_elements.description: An ordered output line produced by applying the template to the address components.

data_elements.name: Rendering context
data_elements.description: Parameters that contextualise rendering, such as origin country, domestic or international posting and target script.

data_elements.name: Unmapped component policy
data_elements.description: Declared behaviour when a component cannot be placed by the destination template.

artifacts.name: Country postal address template
artifacts.description: The machine-processable template that expresses a country's postal address rendering rules, together with its human-readable form and the sample address set used to derive and test it.
artifacts.identity_strategy: Country code plus template identifier and version issued by the publishing body; each edition carries an RFC 3339 publication timestamp.

bundles.name: Spatial position and reference systems
bundles.description: Coordinate positions with their meaning, method and accuracy; the coordinate and geographic-identifier reference systems that give them sense; and non-coordinate code and grid references.
bundles.rationale: ISO 19111 requires a CRS and, for dynamic systems, a coordinate epoch before a coordinate has meaning; INSPIRE requires every geographic position to declare what it specifies, by what method, and whether it is the default; ISO 19112 provides the parallel model for referencing by geographic identifier. GeoJSON and Open Location Code show that encodings impose their own hard constraints.

layers.name: Position, specification and accuracy
layers.description: What a stored coordinate actually points at, how it was obtained, which of several positions is default, and how accurate and how precise it is.

findings.name: Position, geometry specification and method
findings.description: The geometry stored for an address or place, an explicit statement of which real-world feature it specifies (entrance, building, parcel, delivery point, utility connection or segment interpolation), the method by which it was determined, and which position is the default among several.

questions.text: What does this position represent — entrance, building, parcel, postal delivery point, utility connection or street segment interpolation?
By what method was the position determined, and by whom?
Which of several positions is the default, and which position should routing, dispatch and statistics each use?
answer_data: Selection rule when the preferred position is missing

questions.text: In which geometry type and dimensionality is the position expressed, including any vertical or floor-level component?

data_elements.name: Position geometry
data_elements.description: The geometry, normally a point, representing the position of the address or place.

data_elements.name: Geometry specification
data_elements.description: Statement of which feature the position specifies, such as entrance, building, parcel, postal delivery point or segment.

data_elements.name: Geometry method
data_elements.description: How and by whom the position was determined or derived.

data_elements.name: Default position flag
data_elements.description: Whether this position is the default one to use when a consumer expresses no preference.

data_elements.name: Vertical or floor level
data_elements.description: Vertical component or floor level qualifying the position where the address is not at ground level.

findings.inline_only_rationale: A position is an intrinsic, multi-valued attribute of the address or place record rather than a separable document; the evidence for how it was obtained is held by the geocoding result artifact and the accuracy evaluation artifact in adjacent findings.

findings.name: Positional accuracy and meaningful precision
findings.description: The stated accuracy of a position with its measure and confidence, the number of digits that are actually meaningful, containment tests that detect implausible coordinates, and how accuracy travels to consumers that accept only a bare point.

questions.text: What is the stated positional accuracy of this coordinate, under which measure and at what confidence level?
How many decimal places or code digits are meaningful here, and which published digits are spurious precision?
What test rejects a position falling outside the parcel, building footprint or jurisdiction it claims?
How is accuracy conveyed to a consumer whose format carries only a point without metadata?

data_elements.name: Horizontal positional accuracy
data_elements.description: Quantified horizontal accuracy of the position, with unit and measure.

data_elements.name: Accuracy confidence level
data_elements.description: Confidence level at which the accuracy figure holds.

data_elements.name: Meaningful coordinate digits
data_elements.description: Number of decimal places or code digits that carry real information; six decimal degrees corresponds to roughly ten centimetres.

data_elements.name: Containment check result
data_elements.description: Outcome of testing whether the position lies within the geometry it claims to be in.

artifacts.name: Positional accuracy evaluation report
artifacts.description: The record of an accuracy evaluation over a set of positions: method, sample, reference data, measures obtained and containment failures found.
artifacts.identity_strategy: Evaluation run identifier assigned by the evaluating party, with an RFC 3339 execution timestamp and the evaluated dataset version.

layers.name: Coordinate and geographic-identifier reference systems
layers.description: The systems that give positions and identifiers their meaning: coordinate reference systems with datums and epochs, and spatial reference systems using geographic identifiers with their gazetteers.

findings.name: Coordinate reference system, epoch and axis order
findings.description: The declared CRS with its authority code and version, whether it is dynamic and therefore requires a coordinate epoch, the axis order and units in force, any vertical CRS, and the coordinate operation used when transforming for a consumer.

questions.text: In which coordinate reference system is this position expressed, cited by authority code and dataset version?
Is the CRS dynamic, and if so which coordinate epoch applies to the stored coordinates?
What axis order and units apply, and how is that reconciled with encodings that fix longitude before latitude?
answer_data: Axis order as defined by the CRS

questions.text: Which coordinate operation, at what accuracy, is applied when transforming into a consumer's CRS?
Is a vertical or compound CRS declared for any height component, and what is its datum?

data_elements.name: Coordinate reference system
data_elements.description: Reference to the CRS in which coordinates are expressed, cited by authority code.

data_elements.name: Coordinate epoch
data_elements.description: Epoch to which coordinates in a dynamic CRS refer, without which those coordinates are ambiguous.

data_elements.name: Axis order and units
data_elements.description: Order and units of coordinate axes as defined by the CRS or overridden by the encoding.

data_elements.name: Vertical CRS
data_elements.description: Reference to the vertical CRS applying to any height component.

data_elements.name: Coordinate operation
data_elements.description: Reference to the transformation or conversion applied between reference systems, with its stated accuracy.

artifacts.name: Coordinate reference system definition record
artifacts.description: The authoritative definition of a CRS, datum or coordinate operation obtained from a geodetic parameter registry, including area of validity and accuracy, referenced rather than redefined by this model.
artifacts.identity_strategy: Registry authority name plus code plus dataset version; codes are stable while dataset versions change, so both are required.

findings.name: Geographic identifiers, location types and gazetteers
findings.description: Spatial referencing by geographic identifier: the location types a reference system defines, the location instances that populate it, the gazetteer that is custodian of record, complementary coordinate references, and instance lifecycle.

questions.text: Which location types does this spatial reference system define, and what identifier form does each use?
answer_data: Identifier form and syntax per type
Theme or domain of the reference system

questions.text: How do location instances nest, adjoin or overlap, and which of those relationships are recorded?
Which gazetteer is custodian of record for each location type, and over what territory of use?
Does each location instance carry a complementary coordinate reference, and at what geometry level?
How are location instances added, merged, split and retired, and are historic instances retained?

data_elements.name: Location type
data_elements.description: A class of location within the spatial reference system, such as country, municipality or postal area.

data_elements.name: Location instance identifier
data_elements.description: Geographic identifier of an individual location instance of a given location type.

data_elements.name: Gazetteer
data_elements.description: Reference to the gazetteer that holds and maintains the location instances for a location type.

data_elements.name: Parent location instance
data_elements.description: Reference to a location instance within which this instance falls.

data_elements.name: Complementary coordinate reference
data_elements.description: Coordinate position or extent recorded alongside the geographic identifier.

artifacts.name: Gazetteer publication
artifacts.description: The published register of location instances for one or more location types, with identifiers, names, positions or extents, and administrative metadata about the custodian and territory of use.
artifacts.identity_strategy: Gazetteer identifier plus release version; instances are identified by their geographic identifier within the declared location type.

layers.name: Code and grid based location references
layers.description: Derived, non-coordinate references such as open location codes and grid squares that stand in for an address where none exists.

findings.name: Open code and grid location references
findings.description: Code-based location references: the scheme and code length in use, the ground area a length resolves, whether a code is full or shortened and therefore needs a reference location, whether the scheme is openly reversible or vendor-dependent, and its role where no civic address exists.

questions.text: Which code scheme is used, at what code length, and what ground area does that length resolve?
Is the code full or shortened, and if shortened, which reference location is required to recover it?
answer_data: Recovery procedure and its ambiguity risk

questions.text: Is the scheme openly specified and reversible without a proprietary service, or does resolution depend on a vendor?
How does the code relate to the underlying coordinate reference system and to any civic address for the same place?
Where no civic address exists, what governs the use of the code as the operative location reference?
answer_data: Limits on legal or postal use

data_elements.name: Location code value
data_elements.description: The code string identifying an area, including any format separator and padding characters.

data_elements.name: Code scheme
data_elements.description: The scheme that defines the code's alphabet, structure and semantics.

data_elements.name: Code length
data_elements.description: Number of significant digits, which determines the resolved area; padded codes must not be shortened.

data_elements.name: Reference location for short codes
data_elements.description: The location required to recover a full code from a shortened one.

data_elements.name: Scheme openness
data_elements.description: Whether the scheme is openly specified and offline-reversible or dependent on a vendor service.

findings.inline_only_rationale: A code reference is a derived value object computed deterministically from coordinates and a scheme; it carries no document of its own. The governing specification is recorded as an external alignment rather than held as a model artifact.

bundles.name: Named places and toponyms
bundles.description: Points of interest used for orientation and discovery, and the toponyms that name places across languages, scripts and periods of official recognition.
bundles.rationale: Overture's places schema shows that a POI carries identity, multi-level categories, existence confidence and operating status distinct from any address; UNGEGN establishes that geographical names are standardised by national authorities and that multilingual, culturally informed naming matters for administration and emergency response. Both are referencing assets, not attributes of the things they name.

layers.name: Points of interest
layers.description: Named places usable for orientation, discovery and reference, with category, status and confidence.

findings.name: POI identity, category, status and confidence
findings.description: The identifier of a point of interest independent of its operator and name, the taxonomy and level that classify it, its operating status as distinct from opening hours, its resolution to addresses and buildings, and the confidence that it exists at all.

questions.text: Which identifier designates the point of interest independently of its operator, brand and current name?
Which category taxonomy classifies the POI, at which level, and which alternate categories also apply?
What is the operating status of the POI, and when was it last confirmed?
How does the POI resolve to one or more addresses, to a building or unit, and to a brand?
What existence confidence is asserted, on what evidence, and what threshold gates publication?

data_elements.name: POI identifier
data_elements.description: Stable identifier for the point of interest as a referenceable entity.

data_elements.name: POI name
data_elements.description: Recognised names of the place, including primary and common variants with language qualification.

data_elements.name: POI category
data_elements.description: Classification of the place, with primary, alternate and basic-level categories from a declared taxonomy.

data_elements.name: Operating status
data_elements.description: Whether the place is open, temporarily closed or permanently closed, distinct from time-of-day opening hours.

data_elements.name: Existence confidence
data_elements.description: Score between zero and one for the certainty that the place exists; zero is paired with permanent closure.

data_elements.name: POI address
data_elements.description: Reference to one or more addresses at which the place is situated.

artifacts.name: POI catalogue entry
artifacts.description: The catalogue record for a point of interest, including identifier, names, categories, position, status, confidence and per-attribute sources; may originate from an operator's own listing submission.
artifacts.identity_strategy: Catalogue-issued POI identifier under a declared reference scheme; operator-supplied identifiers are retained as alternative identifiers, never as the primary key.

layers.name: Toponyms and multilingual names
layers.description: Place names with their language, script, romanisation, official standardisation status and history.

findings.name: Toponym language, script and official status
findings.description: Which place a toponym names, the language and script of each name form and its relation to a source form, which form is officially standardised by the national names authority, how contested or reinstated names are recorded, and which form to display for a given audience.

questions.text: Which named place does this toponym name, and is the same name borne by other places within the same scope?
In which language and script is each name form recorded, and which forms are romanisations of which source form?
Which form is officially standardised by the national names authority, and which are endonyms, exonyms or historic forms?
How are contested, reinstated or superseded names recorded without erasing prior forms?
Which name form should a consumer display for a stated audience locale, and what is the fallback?

data_elements.name: Toponym
data_elements.description: A name form for the place as written in a specific language and script.

data_elements.name: Name language
data_elements.description: Language of the name form, needed for multilingual and culturally informed naming.

data_elements.name: Name script
data_elements.description: Script in which the name form is written.

data_elements.name: Name status
data_elements.description: Standardisation status of the name form: official, standardised, historic, endonym, exonym or unofficial.

data_elements.name: Romanisation system
data_elements.description: The transliteration or romanisation system used to derive a Latin-script form.

data_elements.name: Names authority
data_elements.description: National or regional names authority that standardised the form.

artifacts.name: Standardised geographical names list
artifacts.description: The national names authority's published list of standardised names with language, script, status and decision references, used as the reference for official display and exchange.
artifacts.identity_strategy: Authority identifier plus publication or release version; individual entries are keyed by the place identifier, not by the name string.

bundles.name: Matching, quality, provenance, access and exchange
bundles.description: How references are resolved and scored, how their quality is tested and defects recorded, where each attribute came from and when, under what licence and protection they may be used, and how they cross into other models and encodings without silent loss.
bundles.rationale: FGDC defines a distinct data quality part and an Address Anomaly Status; Overture records per-attribute sources with confidence and timestamps; W3C and OGC best practice requires published validation schemas, declared accuracy and responsible interaction; ISO 19160-1 exists precisely to enable cross-mapping. These concerns determine whether a reference can be relied upon.

layers.name: Matching, quality tests and anomalies
layers.description: Resolution of input strings and positions to reference records with scored outcomes, and the tests, anomalies and defect handling that keep the register trustworthy.

findings.name: Geocoding and address matching outcomes
findings.description: The normalisation and parsing that precede matching, the reference dataset version matched against, the score and type of a match, the threshold that separates automatic acceptance from review, and the explicit representation of ambiguity, partial matches and interpolation.

questions.text: What normalisation and parsing steps precede matching, and against which reference dataset version was the match run?
What match score, match type and matched component set does the operation return?
Which score threshold accepts a match automatically, and what routes a candidate to human review?
Is the result stored as an attribute of the address or as a separate derived observation with its own timestamp and inputs?
How are ambiguous, partial and interpolated results represented rather than silently resolved to one answer?

data_elements.name: Match score
data_elements.description: Numeric score expressing confidence that the input resolved to the matched reference record.

data_elements.name: Match type
data_elements.description: Kind of match achieved: exact, standardised, partial, interpolated or unmatched.

data_elements.name: Matched address
data_elements.description: Reference to the address record the input resolved to.

data_elements.name: Reference dataset version
data_elements.description: Version of the reference dataset used for matching, without which a result cannot be reproduced.

data_elements.name: Candidate set
data_elements.description: Alternative candidates with their scores, retained when the match is ambiguous.

data_elements.name: Interpolation flag
data_elements.description: Whether the position was interpolated along a segment rather than observed.

artifacts.name: Geocoding or matching result record
artifacts.description: The reproducible record of one matching run: input, normalisation applied, reference dataset version, engine version, candidates, chosen result, score and timestamp.
artifacts.identity_strategy: Run identifier issued by the matching service, combined with the input record key; execution time recorded in RFC 3339 with an explicit offset or Z.

findings.name: Quality tests, anomaly status and defect handling
findings.description: The tests a record must pass — syntax, completeness, conformity to the governing reference system, duplication and positional containment — the anomaly status recorded when it fails, whether an anomalous address remains usable, and how defects are notified and resolved with retained evidence.

questions.text: Which quality tests does this record pass or fail, and against which rule set version were they run?
What anomaly status applies when the address is not correct under its governing reference system, and may it still be used?
answer_data: Anomaly status value or explanatory note

questions.text: Who is notified of a defect, within what period must it be resolved, and what status applies meanwhile?
What evidence is retained to show that a test was executed against a specific record version?
Is the validation rule set published so that consumers can check records before submitting them?
answer_data: Published schema or rule set location

data_elements.name: Quality test
data_elements.description: Identifier of a test applied to the record, drawn from the published rule set.

data_elements.name: Test result
data_elements.description: Outcome of a quality test for the record version tested.

data_elements.name: Address anomaly status
data_elements.description: Status flag or explanatory note for an address that is not correct according to the address reference system that governs it.

data_elements.name: Test execution time
data_elements.description: RFC 3339 timestamp at which the test was executed.

data_elements.name: Published validation schema
data_elements.description: Reference to the online schema or rule set used for validation.

artifacts.name: Quality and conformance test report
artifacts.description: The published outcome of running the declared test suite over a register or delivery, listing measures, failures, anomaly counts and the record versions and rule set versions involved.
artifacts.identity_strategy: Report identifier issued by the testing party plus the dataset version tested; execution timestamps in RFC 3339.

findings.name: Quality elements, measures and reporting
findings.description: ISO 19160-3 is a profile of ISO 19157 that establishes data quality elements and measures for address data, procedures for reporting, and guidelines for use. Elements include completeness, logical consistency, positional accuracy, temporal quality, thematic accuracy and usability. The standard does not define minimum acceptable quality; fitness depends on use.

questions.text: Against which dataset or record scope, product specification and intended use was quality evaluated?
What completeness, logical consistency, positional accuracy, temporal quality, thematic accuracy and usability results were obtained?
When was the evaluation performed, by which method, and is the result still current relative to subsequent updates?
Does the consumer impose a minimum quality threshold that ISO 19160-3 itself does not define, and is that threshold recorded as a local constraint?

data_elements.name: quality-scope
data_elements.description: Dataset, series or record scope of the evaluation

data_elements.name: completeness-result
data_elements.description: Commission and omission measures

data_elements.name: logical-consistency-result
data_elements.description: Conceptual, domain, format and topological consistency

data_elements.name: positional-accuracy-result
data_elements.description: Absolute or relative positional accuracy

data_elements.name: temporal-quality-result
data_elements.description: Temporal accuracy and validity

data_elements.name: thematic-accuracy-result
data_elements.description: Correctness of classification and attributes

data_elements.name: usability-result
data_elements.description: Fitness for a stated use

data_elements.name: evaluated-at
data_elements.description: Quality evaluation time

artifacts.name: Address quality report
artifacts.description: Evaluation results against ISO 19160-3 elements for a stated scope and use
artifacts.identity_strategy: Identified by evaluated scope, product specification and RFC 3339 evaluation time; a new evaluation adds a report rather than altering address identity.

layers.name: Source lineage and attribution of facts
layers.description: Per-attribute lineage, source and ingestion times, contributor rights and precedence when sources disagree.

findings.name: Per-attribute source lineage and observation time
findings.description: Which source dataset and source record contributed each attribute, the separate source-update, ingestion and event times, the rights a contributor retains in what they contributed, and the precedence rule that decides between conflicting sources without discarding the loser.

questions.text: From which source dataset and source record did each attribute of this record derive?
What are the source update time, the ingestion time and the real-world event time for each contributed attribute, and where do they diverge?
Which contributor holds rights in each contributed attribute, and does that constrain redistribution of the merged record?
answer_data: Effect on redistribution of the whole

questions.text: When two sources conflict on the same attribute, which precedence rule decides, and is the rejected value retained?
What confidence does each source attach to its own assertion, and how is that combined into the published record?

data_elements.name: Source dataset
data_elements.description: Reference to a dataset that contributed one or more attributes of the record.

data_elements.name: Source record identifier
data_elements.description: Identifier of the specific record in the source dataset that supplied the value.

data_elements.name: Source update time
data_elements.description: Time at which the source asserted or last updated the value, as an RFC 3339 timestamp.

data_elements.name: Attribute scope of lineage
data_elements.description: The specific attribute or property path to which a lineage entry applies.

data_elements.name: Source precedence rule
data_elements.description: Rule deciding which source wins for a given attribute when sources disagree.

findings.inline_only_rationale: Lineage is carried as per-attribute reference data on each record version, pointing at datasets and records that are themselves owned and published elsewhere. Holding a separate lineage document here would duplicate the register change log and the external source datasets, both already treated as artifacts or external references.

layers.name: Licensing, access and protection
layers.description: The licence and access conditions attached to reference data, and the privacy, safety, suppression and retention constraints that limit its publication.

findings.name: Licence, redistribution and access conditions
findings.description: The licence governing use, redistribution and derivation, licence encumbrance carried in from individual components, the effect of a statutory duty to publish, and the obligations that follow derived geocodes.

questions.text: Under what licence may this dataset be used, redistributed and built upon, and does the licence differ by component?
Which components are encumbered by a third-party licence that blocks open publication of the merged whole?
Does a statutory duty to publish spatial data override or coexist with a commercial licence here?
What attribution, share-alike or field-of-use restriction attaches to geocodes derived from this data?

data_elements.name: Licence
data_elements.description: Reference to the licence under which the reference data is made available.

data_elements.name: Licence scope
data_elements.description: The components, attributes or territories to which a given licence applies.

data_elements.name: Redistribution permitted
data_elements.description: Whether the recipient may redistribute the data or derivatives of it.

data_elements.name: Attribution requirement
data_elements.description: Attribution text or notice that must accompany use or derivation.

artifacts.name: Licence or data use agreement
artifacts.description: The instrument that grants and limits use of the reference dataset, including attribution, redistribution, field-of-use and term.
artifacts.identity_strategy: Licence identifier and version issued by the licensor; agreement instances additionally keyed by contract number and RFC 3339 commencement timestamp.

findings.name: Privacy, safety, suppression and retention
findings.description: When a location reference becomes personal data, which records are suppressed or coarsened for safety and by whose decision, how long records and matching logs are kept, what is deleted versus tombstoned, and how authorised responders still reach a suppressed record.

questions.text: At what point does this location reference become personal data, and which linkage causes that?
Which records are suppressed or coarsened for safety, by whose decision, and for how long?
What precision reduction applies when publishing a sensitive position, and is the reduction reversible from published data?
How long are retired addresses, assignment records and matching logs retained, and what is hard-deleted versus tombstoned?
What lawful-access route allows emergency services or another authorised party to reach a suppressed record?

data_elements.name: Sensitivity class
data_elements.description: Classification governing whether and at what resolution the reference may be published.

data_elements.name: Suppression decision
data_elements.description: Reference to the decision that suppressed or coarsened the record, including its decider and review date.

data_elements.name: Coarsening rule
data_elements.description: Rule reducing published precision for sensitive records, for example truncating code digits or snapping to an area centroid.

data_elements.name: Retention period
data_elements.description: Duration for which a record class is retained before deletion or archival transfer.

data_elements.name: Deletion mode
data_elements.description: Whether expiry results in hard deletion, tombstoning with identifier retention, or archival transfer.

artifacts.name: Suppression or sensitivity decision record
artifacts.description: The decision that classifies a location reference as sensitive and sets the publication constraint, its reviewer, review date and the lawful-access route retained for authorised parties.
artifacts.identity_strategy: Decision number issued by the deciding authority, with RFC 3339 effective and review timestamps; the affected record is referenced by identifier, never by name alone.

layers.name: Crosswalks, conformance and projections
layers.description: Declared mappings to external address models, the evidence behind any conformance claim, and the encoding projections that expose the canonical record.

findings.name: Crosswalks, conformance evidence and encoding projections
findings.description: The external models this register is mapped to and where those mappings lose information, the evidence supporting any conformance claim, the published encoding projections and their derivation from one canonical record, and the handling of components with no target in a receiving model.

questions.text: To which external address or location models is this register crosswalked, at which versions, and where is each mapping lossy?
What evidence supports each claimed conformance class, and was a conformance test actually executed?
Which encoding projections are published, and are they all derived from a single canonical record?
Which fields does each projection drop or default, and is that projection therefore non-authoritative?
How is a component with no target in the receiving model conveyed without silent loss?

data_elements.name: Crosswalk
data_elements.description: Reference to a documented mapping between this model's elements and an external model's elements.

data_elements.name: Target model version
data_elements.description: Version of the external model to which the crosswalk applies.

data_elements.name: Mapping loss note
data_elements.description: Statement of the information lost or defaulted in a given direction of the mapping.

data_elements.name: Conformance claim
data_elements.description: A claimed conformance class against an external standard, valid only when accompanied by test evidence.

data_elements.name: Encoding projection
data_elements.description: Identifier of a published projection of the canonical record into a specific encoding or interface.

artifacts.name: Crosswalk table and conformance evidence pack
artifacts.description: The maintained element-level mapping between this register and an external model, paired with the executed conformance test results that justify any conformance claim.
artifacts.identity_strategy: Crosswalk identifier plus the pair of source and target model versions; each pack carries an RFC 3339 publication timestamp and the test run identifiers it evidences.

functions.name: Assign address
functions.description: Create a new address record binding an address to an addressable object under a governing address reference system, producing an authority decision and an initial lifecycle status.
inputs: Addressable object reference and owning model
outputs: Address record with identifier and lifecycle status
preconditions: The acting authority holds a mandate in force covering the object's location
The proposed designator passes the numbering rules of the governing reference system
The addressable object is resolvable in its owning model
effects: A new address identifier is issued and made resolvable
Lifecycle status is set and status change time recorded in RFC 3339
A new record version is opened in the register change log

functions.name: Retire address
functions.description: Withdraw an address from current use while retaining it for historical resolution, optionally linking to a superseding address.
outputs: Updated address record with retired status
preconditions: The address exists and is not already retired
The acting authority is competent for the address's jurisdiction
Any dependent sub-addresses have a declared cascade outcome
effects: Lifecycle status becomes retired and validity end time is set
Historic resolution remains available for the declared retention period
Downstream consumers are notified through the change log

functions.name: Validate address
functions.description: Test an address record against its governing specification profile and address reference system, returning per-test results and an anomaly status where it fails.
preconditions: The governing profile and reference system are resolvable
The published validation rule set version is known
effects: Anomaly status is set or cleared on the record
A test execution record is retained against the specific record version
Defects are routed to the responsible steward

functions.name: Render postal address
functions.description: Apply a destination country template to stored address components to produce ordered, formatted output lines for postal use.
inputs: Addressee segment supplied by the party model
outputs: Report of components that had no target
preconditions: A template exists for the destination country at a known version
Mandatory components required by the template are present
effects: A rendered representation is produced and may be cached with its template version
Unmapped components are disclosed rather than dropped silently

functions.name: Parse address string
functions.description: Decompose an unstructured address string into typed components and locators under a declared country profile, retaining the original string.
inputs: Assumed country and language or script
preconditions: A parsing profile exists for the assumed country
Character encoding and script of the input are known or detectable
effects: A structured candidate is produced for matching or validation
Residue and low confidence are surfaced instead of being discarded

functions.name: Geocode address
functions.description: Resolve a structured or unstructured address to one or more reference records and positions, returning scored candidates rather than a forced single answer.
outputs: Match score, match type and matched component set
preconditions: The reference dataset version is available and its licence permits the use
Normalisation rules for the territory are defined
effects: A reproducible geocoding result record is written with an RFC 3339 execution timestamp
Ambiguous or interpolated outcomes are flagged for review

functions.name: Reverse geocode position
functions.description: Resolve a coordinate position to candidate addresses, geographic identifiers or points of interest, qualified by distance and the geometry specification of each candidate.
inputs: Position geometry with its CRS and epoch
outputs: Geometry specification of each candidate position
Statement when no candidate meets the tolerance
preconditions: The input CRS is declared and transformable to the reference dataset CRS
Positional accuracy of the input is stated or assumed and disclosed
effects: Candidates are returned with their own accuracy and specification
No candidate is asserted as authoritative beyond its stated confidence

functions.name: Transform position between reference systems
functions.description: Convert or transform a position from one coordinate reference system to another using a declared coordinate operation, preserving epoch and accuracy information.
inputs: Source position with CRS and coordinate epoch
outputs: Transformed position in the target CRS
Operation identifier and its stated accuracy
preconditions: Both CRSs are resolvable from a geodetic parameter registry with a known dataset version
The position lies within the operation's area of validity
A coordinate epoch is present when either CRS is dynamic
effects: Accuracy degradation introduced by the operation is recorded, not hidden
Axis order and units are adjusted to the target CRS or the target encoding

functions.name: Resolve geographic identifier
functions.description: Look up a location instance of a declared location type in a gazetteer, returning its identifier, names, relationships and any complementary coordinate reference.
outputs: Location instance with identifier and names
Complementary position or extent where held
preconditions: The gazetteer is the declared custodian of record for the location type
The territory of use covers the query
effects: Ambiguity across homonyms is surfaced with disambiguating context
Retired instances are returned marked as historic rather than omitted

functions.name: Attach location reference to a host subject
functions.description: Apply this model as a mixin to a subject in another model by recording a typed binding to an address, geographic identifier, position or code reference, with basis, purpose and effective period.
inputs: Host subject identifier and owning model
outputs: Binding record linking subject and location reference
preconditions: The host subject is resolvable in its owning model
The target location reference exists and is not retired, or its historic use is explicitly permitted
The binding purpose is among those the target is authoritative for
effects: The host subject becomes locatable without absorbing referencing semantics
Cardinality and exclusivity rules for the purpose are enforced
The binding is versioned with RFC 3339 effective timestamps

functions.name: Publish reference data release
functions.description: Cut a dated, versioned release of a register, gazetteer or reference dataset together with its licence, validation schema and crosswalk pack, and emit the delta since the previous release.
inputs: Suppression and coarsening rules to apply
outputs: Versioned release artifact with release identifier
Delta or change log since the previous release
Conformance and quality report for the release
preconditions: All records in scope have a current validation result
Suppression decisions in force have been applied
Third-party licence encumbrances permit the intended publication
effects: A citable, serial release exists with an RFC 3339 publication timestamp
Consumers can reproduce a past state by release identifier
Sensitive records are coarsened or withheld per the applied rules

functions.name: Maintain address
functions.description: Modify address components, reassign the address to a different object, or retire it while retaining identifier history.
preconditions: The address exists in the register
effects: Components are modified, the address is reassigned, or the address is retired
Identifier history remains resolvable

functions.name: Rename thoroughfare
functions.description: Record an official thoroughfare name change, preserve former names as aliases, and identify affected addresses without silently changing their master identifiers.
preconditions: The actor is the thoroughfare naming authority
effects: Former names remain resolvable as aliases
Affected addresses are identified without automatic master-identifier change

functions.name: Evaluate address quality
functions.description: Measure completeness, logical consistency, positional accuracy, temporal quality, thematic accuracy and usability for a stated scope and use.
preconditions: An intended use is stated, because no universal minimum quality is defined
effects: Quality results are recorded for the stated scope and use

functions.name: Crosswalk profile
functions.description: Map an address or location record between ISO 19160-1 profiles, INSPIRE, FGDC, CLDXF, locn or postal templates, recording lossiness and conflicts.
preconditions: A documented mapping rule exists between the two profiles
effects: Dropped or unmappable elements are recorded rather than invented

composition.target: Any locatable subject model (host of this mixin)
composition.purpose: Supply address, geographic identifier, position and code-reference capability to any subject that must state where it is, without the host absorbing addressing authority, lifecycle or reference-system semantics.
Bind addresses to buildings as addressable objects; the address record carries the reference while the building model owns the structure, its geometry and its condition.

composition.target: Premises and spatial unit model (legacy U2)
composition.purpose: Resolve sub-address locators — building, floor, unit, room and seat levels — to spatial units defined and governed by the premises model.

composition.target: Land parcel and cadastre model (legacy P2)
composition.purpose: Bind addresses to parcels where no building stands, and support positional containment tests against parcel geometry, without importing tenure or rights.

composition.target: Administrative units and settlements model (legacy U4)
composition.purpose: Resolve administrative unit name and address area name components to authoritative administrative units and named places rather than repeating their names as free text.
Link thoroughfare names used for addressing to the transport link features that carry centreline geometry and network topology.

composition.target: Public mandate and authority model (legacy A12)
composition.purpose: Resolve the addressing authority and its mandate instrument, jurisdiction extent and effective period, which condition the validity of every assignment act.
Supply the addressee and organisation segments needed to render a complete postal address at run time, while keeping party identity outside this model.

composition.target: Geodetic parameter registry (external CRS and coordinate operation authority)
composition.purpose: Resolve coordinate reference systems, datums, epochs and coordinate operations by authority code and dataset version instead of redefining them.

Align the address record, its components, aliases, lifecycle attributes and metadata with the international conceptual address model, and use its cross-mapping intent as the basis for declared crosswalks rather than assumed equivalence.

composition.target: ISO 19160-4:2023 international postal address components and template language, with UPU S42
composition.purpose: Align postal components, sub-elements, rendering rules and country templates; note that S42 Part A and Part B are the operational carrier of country templates.

composition.target: ISO 19112:2019 Spatial referencing by geographic identifiers
composition.purpose: Align location types, location instances, gazetteers and complementary coordinate references so that identifier-based referencing is modelled to the same schema as the coordinate-based path.

composition.target: INSPIRE Addresses application schema 4.0 and Regulation (EU) No 1089/2010
composition.purpose: Align address component subtypes, locator structure, geographic position specification and the split between real-world validity and record version lifespan with the binding European schema.

composition.target: FGDC-STD-016-2011 United States Thoroughfare, Landmark, and Postal Address Data Standard
composition.purpose: Align address classes, lifecycle status values, address authority lineage and the anomaly-against-reference-system concept; treat it as a national profile, not a universal one.

composition.target: IETF RFC 5139 civic location format and NENA-STA-004.2-2024 CLDXF-US
composition.purpose: Align civic address element decomposition for emergency location exchange, and adopt the documented FGDC-to-CLDXF crosswalk pattern as evidence that mappings must be maintained explicitly.
Constrain the position projection: WGS 84 in decimal degrees, longitude before latitude, cut antimeridian geometries, and avoid publishing precision beyond what accuracy supports.
Fix the encoding of every timestamp in the model, including the explicit-offset requirement and the -00:00 convention for an unknown local offset.

composition.target: W3C and OGC Spatial Data on the Web Best Practices
composition.purpose: Adopt persistent identifiers for spatial things, declared coordinate reference systems, described positional accuracy, published validation schemas, change information for spatial things, and responsible interaction with spatial data.

Extend the model's reference kinds with an openly specified, offline-reversible code scheme for places without civic addresses, while recording that shortened codes are not self-contained identifiers.

composition.target: UNGEGN national names authorities and standardised names lists
composition.purpose: Align toponym language, script, romanisation and standardisation status with nationally standardised names, and treat names authority decisions as the authority for official display forms.

owner_package_requirements: An adopting Dimension must name a single accountable address registrar or reference-data steward, and record the mandate instrument, jurisdiction extent and effective period that authorise assignment and retirement within its scope.

It must declare, per territory it operates in, the governing address specification profile, the address reference systems in force, the coordinate reference systems and their dataset versions, and the gazetteers it treats as custodian of record — each by identifier and version, not by name alone.

It must publish its validation rule set, its crosswalks with versions and known losses, its licence and access conditions, and its retention and suppression rules before publishing any address, position or place record.
dimension.namespace_guidance: Use a stable namespace for this model that separates the reference (address, thoroughfare, geocode, reference system, location instance, place, toponym) from the referent, so that a host subject can carry a location reference without inheriting its namespace. Identifiers minted by the Dimension must be namespaced by issuing register and never reuse a retired value; identifiers imported from an external authority keep that authority's namespace and are recorded as alternative identifiers rather than rewritten. Territory-specific profiles belong in sub-namespaces so that two national profiles can coexist without collision.
registry_links: Vercy registry entry vr.wm-xct-010 (WM-XCT-010, Location Referencing / Address), navigation path NAV.XCT.LOC, entry kind mixin
External geodetic parameter registry for coordinate reference systems, datums and coordinate operations, cited by authority code and dataset version
